flags.reason: Hand-written sample for the Designer / Agent views. The pack pipeline did not produce or check this entry.
The types accept any node in leading; only Icon is verified in the evidence. Do not read this as a limit.

summary: Use a Badge to make a short status, category, or count easy to scan beside the content it describes.

useWhen.text: A short status, category, or count describes nearby content.

from.quote: Use a Badge to make a short status, category, or count easy to scan beside the content it describes.
Avoid a sentence inside the Badge

anatomy.holds: An optional Icon before the label.

from.quote: Adds a recognizable cue without replacing the words.

anatomy.holds: The status, category, or count text.

from.quote: Names the status or category.

anatomy.holds: The token-owned shape around the label.

from.quote: Groups the message into one compact shape.

placementAdvice.text: Place the Badge beside its subject, such as next to a row title.

from.quote: Keep status beside its subject

placementAdvice.text: Pass the Badge's own modes object to an Icon in leading.

from.quote: It renders a supplied leading node verbatim, so the guide passes the same owner mode object to the public Icon and selects the matching `Context4` for Solid or Glass.

configuration.text: Use the solid type beside ordinary content.

from.quote: Use a solid Badge beside ordinary content.

configuration.text: Use the glass type only where the image or surface underneath stays part of the composition.

from.quote: Use glass where the underlying image or surface remains part of the composition.

configuration.text: Choose Badge Size for the density of the surrounding content.
Give High emphasis only to the status that needs attention.

from.quote: Give the status needing attention the strongest emphasis.

rules.text: Write the status in a few familiar words, not a sentence.

from.quote: Write the status, not a sentence

rules.text: Keep tense and capitalization consistent across a set of badges.

from.quote: Keep tense and capitalization consistent across the same set.

states.when: The default. The Badge only shows information.

from.quote: Most badges communicate information.

states.when: Only when opening related detail is useful. Pass onPress.

from.quote: Add an action only when opening related detail is useful.

states.when: While the value is still arriving. Pass loading.

from.quote: Loading shows that the value is still arriving.

accessibility.text: Write a meaningful visible label. Badge ignores accessibilityLabel, so the label is its accessible name.

from.quote: The current Badge implementation ignores its `accessibilityLabel` argument on the rendered wrapper; the interactive example keeps a meaningful visible label.

doDont.do: Use a short status, such as Paid.
doDont.dont: Put the whole explanation inside the Badge.

from.quote: Avoid putting the whole explanation inside the Badge.

doDont.do: Match the system meaning to the words.
doDont.dont: Show Paid as negative or Failed as positive.
doDont.why: Conflicting words and tone make the status harder to trust.

from.quote: Conflicting words and tone make the status harder to trust.

doDont.do: Reserve High emphasis for the status that needs attention.
doDont.dont: Give every status the same High emphasis.
doDont.why: If every status competes, the urgent one is harder to find.

from.quote: If every status competes, the urgent one is harder to find.

examples.purpose: A status beside a row title
examples.jsx:
<Card variant="slim" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
  <HStack alignVertical="center" justifyHorizontal="space-between" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
    <Text>September payment</Text>
    <Badge
      label="Paid"
      modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', 'Badge Size': 'Medium', 'Semantic Intent': 'System', AppearanceSystem: 'positive', Emphasis: 'High', Context4: 'Badge' }}
    />
  </HStack>
</Card>

from.quote: Place the compact status next to the item it describes.

examples.purpose: A leading Icon that shares the Badge's modes
examples.jsx:
<Badge
  label="New"
  leading={
    <Icon
      iconName="ic_card"
      accessibilityElementsHidden
      importantForAccessibility="no"
      modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', 'Badge Size': 'Medium', 'Semantic Intent': 'Brand', AppearanceBrand: 'Primary', Emphasis: 'High', Context4: 'Badge' }}
    />
  }
  modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', 'Badge Size': 'Medium', 'Semantic Intent': 'Brand', AppearanceBrand: 'Primary', Emphasis: 'High', Context4: 'Badge' }}
/>

from.quote: Adds a recognizable cue without replacing the words.

examples.purpose: An action that opens related detail
examples.jsx:
<Badge

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label text shown inside the badge.

props.name: modes
props.description: Modes used to resolve design tokens.

props.name: leading
props.description: Optional node rendered before the label, inside the surface.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a badge-shaped skeleton instead of the badge.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accepted by the types, but ignored when rendered. See gaps.

modes.name: Context4
modes.description: Badge for the solid type, Badge/glass for glass.

slots.name: leading
slots.description: Rendered verbatim; it does not receive the Badge's modes.
